messages:
tina: Hey folks, first-day environment weirdness. On an M1 Mac (macOS 14) trying to bootstrap dev box with asdf (nodejs, python, rust). Node installed fine but Python 3.11 via asdf fails when pip builds wheels for cryptography and psycopg2 with errors about OpenSSL and clang. Rust crate compilation also erroring out complaining about linker. Any quick gotchas for Apple Silicon we should know?

jake: welcome! common checklist: 1) Xcode CLI tools, 2) brew under /opt/homebrew, 3) openssl and pkg-config from brew, 4) ensure asdf is sourced early. Which errors exactly for cryptography? often it's "unable to find OpenSSL" or a clang link error.

tina: error snippet: "error: can't find OpenSSL lib" and later "ld: library not found for -lssl" when building wheels. Also pip tries to compile instead of using prebuilt wheel.

lina: for wheels you want the build deps. On Apple Silicon do this:
```bash
# xcode tools
xcode-select --install
# homebrew and libs
brew install openssl@1.1 pkg-config libffi
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"
export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib/pkgconfig"
# then reinstall python env
asdf uninstall python 3.11.6 || true
asdf install python 3.11.6
python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
pip install -r requirements.txt
```
That resolves the OpenSSL locate for most people.

tina: thanks — do I need to recompile python itself against brew openssl?

jake: asdf's python build (which uses python-build under the hood) picks up those flags if present at build time. If you installed python via asdf before installing openssl pkg, re-installing that python version (asdf uninstall/install) helps.

tina: rust errors were like "linker `cc` not found" or "ld: symbol(s) not found" when building native extensions.

lina: ensure cargo/rustup is installed via rustup (not brew) for predictable toolchain and that Xcode CLT is installed. Also export PATH so /opt/homebrew/bin is first so we use brew clang/cc if needed. If you have Rosetta brew under /usr/local and Arm brew under /opt/homebrew, prefer the latter for arm64 builds. For occasional binary incompatibilities you can pass --platform manylinux or use universal2 wheels, but usually fixing OpenSSL+CLT is enough.

jake: small dotfiles notes: our org uses a starter dotfiles repo (org/dotfiles-starter). Run ./setup.sh which symlinks configs with stow. Don't put secrets (API tokens) in the repo. Use direnv for project-level env vars and the macOS Keychain for long-lived tokens. Example direnv .envrc snippet we use at work:
```bash
export REDWOOD_DEV=1
export REPO_TOKEN=\"$(security find-generic-password -s redwood-repo -w)\"
```
This way you don't commit tokens.

tina: where should I put the LDFLAGS/CPPFLAGS? zshrc or zprofile?

lina: put PATH and brew-related exports in ~/.zprofile so GUI apps/Integrated terminals see them. You can put interactive stuff in ~/.zshrc. Important: source asdf in whichever file is read early: e.g. in ~/.zprofile add `.` $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh so asdf shims are in PATH for login shells.

jake: FYI if pip is still trying to compile wheels for cryptography you can pin a wheel-friendly version or enable the prebuilt wheel: `pip install cryptography --prefer-binary` while you sort libs.

tina: my dotfiles setup script failed with permission denied when stow tried to symlink into /usr/local etc. Any advice?

lina: avoid touching /usr/local unless necessary. If something in the repo tries to change /usr/local, check the setup script and fix paths to /opt/homebrew. If you installed some tools under legacy /usr/local (from Rosetta), you might need to migrate to /opt/homebrew. Use `brew doctor` to surface problems.

tina: awesome, thanks! I'll try reinstalling python via asdf after brew openssl install and post any follow-ups here. Appreciate the tips.
